issues.failure_explanation: From the definition, R_theta(Z + c) = R_theta(Z) + c for every constant c (cash invariance), so R_theta is affine along the direction of constant random variables and hence convex but not strictly convex. The intro asserts strict convexity for every fixed theta, which is false.

failure_location.quote: Furthermore, for each fixed parameter, it is strictly convex and smooth.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace 'strictly convex' by 'convex' (or state strict convexity only modulo constants).
issues.overall_effect: Only the introductory characterization is wrong; uniqueness of the optimal control is correctly derived later from the lambda-penalty, not from strict convexity of R.
issues.title: Entropic risk measure is not strictly convex
issues.why_classification: Local wording correction; no result relies on the false property.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof's bound rho <= 1 - 2 tau c + 2 tau^2 L^2 + 4 sqrt(eta) + 8 eta is < 1 iff 4 sqrt(eta)+8 eta < 2 tau c - 2 tau^2 L^2. The right-hand side is tau-dependent, tends to 0 as tau -> 0, and is strictly smaller than c^2/(2L^2) for every tau in the open interval (0, c/(2L^2)) (the value c^2/(2L^2) is attained only at the excluded endpoint). Hence the stated tau-independent condition 4 sqrt(eta)+8 eta < c^2/(2L^2) does not imply rho < 1 for every tau in (0, c/(2L^2)); e.g. for tau small, rho > 1.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the condition by 4 sqrt(eta) + 8 eta < 2 tau c - 2 tau^2 L^2 (eta sufficiently small depending on tau), which gives rho < 1 for the chosen tau.
issues.overall_effect: As stated, the theorem's quantifier 'for every tau in (0, c/(2L^2))' with a fixed eta-condition is false; linear convergence holds only under a tau-dependent smallness condition on eta.
issues.title: Contraction condition on eta in Theorem 3.1 is not sufficient for every admissible tau
issues.why_classification: A one-line correction of the smallness condition restores the proof; the linear convergence conclusion and rate type are unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: Each single-level sample Y_ell^(m) >= 1, but the MLMC estimator is a telescoping sum whose level corrections Delta Y_ell^(m) = Y_ell^(m) - Y_{ell-1}^(m) can be negative. Hence E^ML[Y_L] is not almost surely > 1; it can be smaller than 1 and even nonpositive with positive probability. The proof divides by E[Y] E^ML[Y_L] and needs a deterministic lower bound on E^ML[Y_L] to obtain the constant C = ||E[X]||^2 / E[Y]^2 and the factor 1 in front of the second term. Without it the bound (and even finiteness of the conditional second moment of the ratio estimator) is not established.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Modify the estimator (e.g. replace the denominator by max{1, E^ML[Y_L]}, which cannot increase |E[Y]-denominator| since E[Y] >= 1) or otherwise establish a lower bound on the denominator (e.g. via a high-probability/conditioning argument), and re-derive the proposition accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The MSE bound of the gradient estimator, and hence the complexity theorem and the idealized complexity corollary built on it, are unsupported for the estimator as defined.
issues.title: Proposition 3.2 assumes the MLMC denominator estimator exceeds 1, which is false
issues.why_classification: A contained modification of the estimator or an additional lemma restores the bound and all downstream complexity results with the same rates, but it is not a routine local fix and changes the analyzed estimator.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: there exist a positive constant $\alpha$, such that for every $\theta\in\mathbb{R}^+$, there exists two positive constants

issues.failure_explanation: The invoked MLMC complexity theorem requires the relation alpha >= (1/2) min(beta, gamma) between weak and strong/cost rates; the theorem here allows arbitrary positive alpha, beta, gamma and invokes the cited result outside its stated hypotheses.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis alpha >= min(beta,gamma)/2 to the theorem (and hence to the corollary).
issues.overall_effect: The cost bound (eq:cost_asymptotic) is unsupported in the regime alpha < min(beta,gamma)/2.
issues.title: Complexity theorem omits the standard MLMC hypothesis alpha >= min(beta,gamma)/2
issues.why_classification: Adding a standard hypothesis restores the invoked result; the rates and conclusions are unchanged in the intended regime.

issues.failure_explanation: With e_k := rho^k and K = |2 log eps / log rho|, one has e_K = rho^K = eps^2, not eps. Moreover e_k bounds the mean-square target (varepsilon_k^2), so Theorem 3.5 gives per-step cost e_k^{-1} (resp. e_k^{-1-(gamma-beta)/(2 alpha)}), not e_k^{-2} (resp. e_k^{-2-(gamma-beta)/alpha}) as written. The two errors cancel to give the stated conclusion, but the displayed chain of inequalities is incorrect as written (taken literally it yields eps^{-4}).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the per-step costs by e_k^{-1}, e_k^{-1}|log e_k|^2, e_k^{-1-(gamma-beta)/(2alpha)} and conclude with e_K ≅ eps^2.
issues.overall_effect: The stated complexity of the idealized algorithm is correct, but its proof as written is invalid.
issues.title: Inconsistent exponents in the proof of the idealized complexity corollary
issues.why_classification: Routine local correction of exponents; the corollary's statement survives unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: With V_ell := v^2/(M-1) the sample variance and M_ell = lambda sqrt(V_ell/C_ell), the MLMC variance is sum V_ell/M_ell = (1/lambda) sum sqrt(V C). The formula uses lambda = (2 eps_k^2)^{-1} sum sqrt(V C), giving variance 2 eps_k^2, i.e. four times the stated target eps_k^2/2 (Giles' formula requires lambda = 2 eps^{-2} sum sqrt(V C)).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace (sqrt(2) eps_k)^{-2} by 2 eps_k^{-2} (or restate the target as 2 eps_k^2).
issues.overall_effect: The adaptive batch sizes produced by the algorithm are systematically a factor 4 too small for the advertised target; the sampling error enforced is 2 eps_k^2 instead of eps_k^2/2.
issues.title: Optimal batch-size formula does not meet its stated sampling-error target
issues.why_classification: Constant-factor correction of a formula; asymptotic rates and method are unaffected.

issues.failure_explanation: Under the weak-error assumption E[Delta_ell] ≈ c h_ell^alpha, the level-L correction is E[Delta_L] ≈ E[Delta_ell] (h_L/h_ell)^alpha, so the bias extrapolated from level ell should be |E Delta_ell| (h_L/h_ell)^alpha / (2^alpha - 1). The estimator instead divides by (h_L/h_ell)^{alpha} < 1, i.e. multiplies by (h_ell/h_L)^alpha, inflating the coarse-level contributions by (h_ell/h_L)^{2 alpha}; with the max over ell this is dominated by the coarsest level and grossly overestimates the bias, triggering spurious refinement.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the factor (h_L/h_ell)^{alpha-hat} in the denominator by (h_ell/h_L)^{alpha-hat} (equivalently multiply the numerator by (h_L/h_ell)^{2 alpha-hat}).
issues.overall_effect: The level-update rule (eq:optimal-level) driven by this estimator does not implement the intended bias control.
issues.title: Bias estimator extrapolates in the wrong direction
issues.why_classification: Single local correction of the estimator formula; the adaptive strategy and guarantees otherwise survive.

issues.failure_explanation: Theorem 3.1 requires the gradient MSE at step k to be bounded by eta ||R_tau(u_k)||^2, the reduced projected gradient, which vanishes at u^*. The algorithm instead sets the accuracy target eps_k = eta ||grad J^ML(u_k)|| and stops when ||grad J^ML(u_k)|| <= eps. For a constrained problem with active constraints at u^*, only the variational inequality holds and ||grad J(u^*)|| > 0 in general, so eps_k does not decay to zero (the enforced tolerance stays bounded below), condition (eq:conditionmeansquareerror) is not implemented, and the while loop cannot terminate for small eps.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace ||grad J^ML(u_k)|| in the stopping rule and in eps_k by the estimated projected gradient (1/tau)||u_k - Pi(u_k - tau grad J^ML(u_k))||.
issues.overall_effect: The implemented algorithm does not realize the hypothesis of Theorem 3.1 in the constrained setting the paper is stated for; its termination criterion is ill-suited when constraints are active.
issues.title: Algorithm's stopping and accuracy rules use the unprojected gradient norm, not the projected gradient of the theory
issues.why_classification: A local substitution in two lines of the algorithm aligns it with the theory without changing the method or its guarantees.
